title: Two of the three main Chhau styles use masks
body: The eastern Indian dance tradition of Chhau has styles from Seraikella, Purulia and Mayurbhanj. Dancers wear masks in the first two styles. Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed with the face uncovered.
takeaway: A shared dance tradition can tell related stories using different ways of showing character.
source: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Chhau Dance (2010)
visual: a brightly painted Chhau mask resting on a wooden stand

title: A Kerala dance drama begins with a picture made on the floor
body: Before Mudiyettu, performers draw a large image of the goddess Kali, called a kalam, on the ground with coloured powders. The image forms part of the preparation for the village's ritual drama.
takeaway: An artwork can be part of what a community does before a performance, rather than an object kept afterwards.
visual: a hand sprinkling coloured powder along a large floor design

title: Mariachi songs carry local history in several languages
body: Mexico's mariachi tradition combines singing with instruments such as strings and trumpets. Its songs can pass on stories about local history in Spanish and in Indigenous languages of western Mexico.
takeaway: The repertoire can preserve how regions tell their own stories, even when the ensemble format travels widely.
visual: a small group of musicians with trumpets and string instruments in a Mexican courtyard
